data.name: Ekavir
data.gender_notes: Ekavir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ekavir is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Eka' meaning one and 'Vir' meaning God or hero. This name signifies being one with the divine and having the qualities of a hero. The name Ekavir carries the meaning “One with God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekavir usually hope their child will grow to embody one with god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ekavir belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One with God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekavir total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ekavir is associated with the Hindu deity Krishna who is also known as Ekadashi Avatar meaning the 'One-Eleventh' avatar. Ekadashi is the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight and is believed to be an auspicious day to seek the blessings of Lord Vishnu. Devotees observe fasting and other rituals on this day. The name Ekavir could be seen as a reminder of the connection between the individual and the divine, reflecting the spiritual and cultural traditions of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: Ekavir symbolizes the pursuit of oneness with the divine. The name itself signifies being one with God, as the name consists of the words 'Eka' meaning one and 'Vir' meaning God. The name serves as a constant reminder to strive towards spiritual growth and self-realization. By connecting ourselves to the divine and having the qualities of a hero, we can face life's challenges with courage, determination, and grace. The pursuit of oneness with the divine is a fundamental tenet of many spiritual traditions and is especially significant in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ekavir, meaning 'One Forest', symbolizes the unity and interconnectedness of all life forms in nature. It emphasizes living in harmony with nature and understanding the inherent oneness of existence.

historical_references.reference: Ekavir is also known as 'Ekadash Ruddra' and is considered as an incarnation of Lord Shiva. He is believed to have appeared to destroy the demon king, Jalandhar, who had taken the form of a Yogini and was deceiving his wife Prakriti. Prakriti had been unaware of Jalandhar's true form, as Lord Shiva had granted him a boon that he could not be killed by a man or a woman. Ekavir, however, was neither a man nor a woman and was therefore able to destroy Jalandhar. This event occurred during the Mahabharata period, around the 4th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Ekavir is an incarnation of Lord Shiva who destroyed the demon king Jalandhar, who had taken the form of a Yogini and was deceiving his wife Prakriti.

historical_references.reference: Ekavir is also mentioned in the Puranic texts as a form of Lord Shiva, who is worshipped to protect against diseases, especially smallpox. He is believed to have appeared during an epidemic in the city of Pragjyotisha (present day Dhaka, Bangladesh) and cured the people by defeating the demon Sambasura. This event is believed to have occurred around the 7th century CE.
historical_references.context: Ekavir is a form of Lord Shiva who is worshipped to protect against diseases, especially smallpox, and appeared during an epidemic in the city of Pragjyotisha to defeat the demon Sambasura.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ekavir' is derived from Hindu mythology and translates to 'One Forest'. In modern context, this name is popularly used on social media platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and Pinterest for promoting yoga, spiritualism, and self-improvement. This is reflected in the hashtag #EkavirYoga and the creation of pages and boards dedicated to this theme.
